contract.reader: A programmer who has read the earlier entries and needs to run a computation across machines that share no memory
contract.problem: Writing correct MPI exchanges and predicting how far a distributed stencil computation scales
contract.outcome: Write exchanges that cannot deadlock; fit and use the latency-bandwidth model; estimate collective costs; decompose a grid with ghost cells; predict strong and weak scaling
contract.contribution: A measured size-dependent deadlock explained by the eager limit, a two-protocol fit of a real ping-pong, and a scaling model checked by its own printed numbers
contract.evidence: Measured Open MPI programs with output; Python models; Hockney, Culler et al., Thakur, Rabenseifner and Gropp, Patarasuk and Yuan, Gropp, Lusk and Skjellum, MPI 4.1 and 5.0
contract.limitations: Messages are shared-memory copies on one machine; cluster figures assumed; contention, topology and noise discussed but not modeled

findings.location: Section 3.3 fit output and Section 5.3 comparison output; desktop-light
findings.problem: Output lines are cut at 1280 px; the measured/model ratio of each fit is hidden
findings.whyItMatters: The next paragraph discusses those ratios (2.33 and 1.22); the reader cannot see the column without the sideways scroll
findings.action: Shorten the printed labels or put the ratio on its own line, and re-run so the output stays genuine
findings.acceptance: Every line of both output blocks visible to its end at 1280 px
